title: Your own split
topic: Split your savings with your bank data

steps.title: Your emergency fund, and the rest
steps.body: Many people split their savings into two parts. First, a few months of costs, ready any day. This part is the [[emergency-fund]]. Second, money that can wait for years. If that part stays in savings, [[inflation]] makes it buy less whenever the interest is lower than the price rise.

steps.prompt: Why do people count an emergency fund in months of costs, not as a round amount?
options: The fund has to pay for life while an income is missing
steps.explanation: An emergency fund buys time. Months of costs tell you how much time it buys.

steps.prompt: True or false: money kept in a savings account for 20 years keeps its value, because the balance never falls.
steps.explanation: False. The balance never falls, but prices rise. If the interest stays lower than [[inflation]], the money buys less each year.

steps.title: Your savings today
steps.body: You have **{totalAssets}** with us. **{savingsShareOfAssets}** of it is in your savings account, at **{savingsRate}** interest a year. That covers about **{bufferMonths}** months of your costs.

steps.title: Your decision
steps.body: Your savings account holds **{savingsBalance}**. How much of it do you want to keep ready any day? The rest is money that can wait. You decide. This app explains how money works. It does not recommend products.
steps.bodyNoData: How much of your savings do you want to keep ready any day? The rest is money that can wait. You decide. This app explains how money works. It does not recommend products.
